items.entity: downward force near the top-right of the square domain
items.description: Results, 'Compliance minimization', Fig. 2a paragraph: 'A force downward is applied at the top right edge'. The exact spot is only drawn in Fig. 2a. A plain square has no 'top right edge', so this could be the top-right corner (top of the symmetry line, like a classic half-MBB beam), the right end of the top edge, or the top end of the right (symmetry) edge.
readings: Top-right corner node (x = 1.0L, y = 1.0L), on the symmetry line
Right end of the top boundary, x in [0.75L, 1.0L] at y = L (last element edge)
Top end of the right/symmetry boundary, y in [0.75L, 1.0L] at x = L

items.entity: downward force near the top-right of the square domain
items.description: The phrase 'applied at the top right edge' suggests a line load on a boundary segment. But the same paragraph equates the objective with 'the vertical displacement where the external force is applied', which suggests a single point. The text doesn't say whether it is a point force or a distributed traction, or how long the loaded segment is (Fig. 2a only).
readings: Concentrated force at a single node
Uniform line load over one element edge (length 0.25L)
Uniform line load over the right half of the top edge (length 0.5L)

items.description: No force value or line-load intensity is given anywhere in the text. Because Eq. (4) divides by the energy of the uniform rho = 0.5 design, the magnitude cancels out of the reported values.
readings: Unit total force F = 1
Unit line-load intensity (force per unit length) over the loaded segment
Any physical value, e.g. 1 kN

items.description: Same paragraph: 'the bottom left edge is set as a roller (no vertical displacement)'. The text doesn't say whether this is just the bottom-left corner point or a segment of the bottom boundary, or how long that segment is. Only Fig. 2a shows it.
readings: Single node at the bottom-left corner (x = 0, y = 0), u_y = 0
Bottom-boundary segment x in [0, 0.25L] (one element edge, 2 nodes), u_y = 0
Bottom-boundary segment x in [0, 0.5L] (left half, 3 nodes), u_y = 0

items.entity: square design domain (half-model, symmetric about the right edge)
items.description: Only 'a square domain' is stated. No side length or out-of-plane thickness is given. With a fixed force these only scale the energy, and they cancel out of the normalized value in Eq. (4).
readings: Unit square L = 1 with unit thickness
Any physical side length (e.g. 0.1 m or 1 m) with arbitrary thickness

items.description: Eq. (6) uses Y0 only as a symbol; no value is given.
readings: Y0 = 1 (normalized)
Y0 = 200 GPa (steel)
Y0 = 70 GPa (aluminium)

items.description: Poisson's ratio is not given anywhere for the compliance problems. The Methods only say the finite element analysis was done in COMSOL 5.4.

items.entity: void/minimum stiffness epsilon in the SIMP law (Eq. 6)
items.description: Eq. (6): 'epsilon is a small number to avoid numerical singularity'. No value or ratio to Y0 is given.
readings: epsilon = 1e-9 * Y0
epsilon = 1e-6 * Y0
epsilon = 1e-3 * Y0

items.entity: 2D elasticity assumption (plane stress vs plane strain)
items.description: The 2D elasticity model (run in COMSOL) does not say whether it is plane stress or plane strain. This changes the effective Poisson ratio and the stiffness level.
readings: Plane stress
Plane strain

items.entity: finite element type/order on the 4x4 mesh
items.description: 'a square domain is divided evenly by a 4x4 mesh' and the Methods line 'the meshes of FEM are the same as the design variables' (COMSOL 5.4) fix 16 square elements, but not their order. On such a coarse mesh, linear and quadratic elements give very different bending stiffness.
readings: 4-node bilinear quadrilaterals (Q4)
8-node quadratic serendipity quadrilaterals
9-node quadratic Lagrange quadrilaterals

items.entity: mapping of the 25 nodal densities to element stiffness
items.description: Eq. (6) and Methods Eq. (17): the nodal densities are interpolated bilinearly and the SIMP law is applied point by point to rho(x). The quadrature used to integrate element stiffness with this varying modulus is not stated. A structured-grid solver that uses one density per element has to choose how to reproduce this.
readings: SIMP evaluated at 2x2 Gauss points of each element from the bilinear nodal interpolation
Higher-order (3x3 or more) Gauss quadrature, effectively exact integration of rho(x)^3
Element density = mean of its 4 nodal values, SIMP applied once per element (constant modulus per element)

items.description: Eq. (5) and the Methods ('weight of linear Gaussian quadrature') define the 0.5 limit through a weight vector w that is never written out. The weighting decides how much volume edge and corner nodes count for.
readings: Exact integral of the bilinear field (trapezoidal weights normalized to sum 1): corner nodes 1/64, edge nodes 1/32, interior nodes 1/16
Uniform weights of 1/25 per node (plain mean of the nodal values)

items.description: No density or sensitivity filter is mentioned for the compliance problems. A Helmholtz filter is described only for the heat problem's 'Approximated' baseline (Methods). On a 4x4 mesh, any filter radius of about one element or more would change the result.
readings: No filter (only the nodal bilinear interpolation)
Density filter with radius 1.5 element widths (0.375L)
Helmholtz/PDE filter with radius half the node spacing (0.125L), copying the heat-problem baseline

items.entity: starting design and settings of the reference MMA run
items.description: The MMA reference run (Fig. 2d, normalized energy 0.293) used COMSOL with optimality tolerance 0.001 (Methods). The starting design, move limits and iteration cap are not given. SIMP with penalty exponent 3 is non-convex, so the starting point can change which local optimum is reached.
readings: Uniform starting density 0.5 (equal to the volume fraction and the reference design)
Uniform starting density 1.0
Random starting design that meets the volume constraint, generated like SOLO's initial batch
